title: 1 Corinthians 1: chapter overview
paragraphs: A salutation and thanksgiving.
Exhortation to brotherly love, and reproof for divisions.
The doctrine of a crucified Saviour, as advancing the glory of God,
and humbling the creature before him.

context: The Corinthian church contained some Jews, but more Gentiles, and the apostle had to contend with the superstition of the one, and the sinful conduct of the other.

title: 1 Corinthians 2: chapter overview
paragraphs: The plain manner in which the apostle preached Christ crucified.
The wisdom contained in this doctrine.
It cannot be duly known but by the Holy Spirit.

title: 1 Corinthians 3: chapter overview
paragraphs: The Corinthians reproved for their contentions.
The true servants of Christ can do nothing without him.
He is the only foundation, and every one should take heed what he builds thereon.
The churches of Christ ought to be kept pure, and to be humble.
And they should not glory in men, because ministers and all things else are theirs through Christ.

paragraphs: Cautions against going to law in heathen courts.
Sins which, if lived and died in, shut out from the kingdom of God.
Our bodies, which are the members of Christ, and temples of the Holy Ghost, must not be defiled.

title: 1 Corinthians 7: chapter overview
paragraphs: The apostle answers several questions about marriage.
Married Christians should not seek to part from their unbelieving consorts.
Persons, in any fixed station, should usually abide in that.
It was most desirable, on account of the then perilous days, for people to sit loose to this world.
Great prudence be used in marriage; it should be only in the Lord.

title: 1 Corinthians 10: chapter overview

Cautions against all idolatrous, and other sinful practices.
The partaking in idolatry cannot exist with having communion with Christ.
All we do to be to the glory of God, and without offence to the consciences of others.

title: 1 Corinthians 11: chapter overview
paragraphs: The apostle, after an exhortation to follow him,
corrects some abuses.
Also contentions, divisions, and disorderly celebrations of the Lord's supper.
He reminds them of the nature and design of its institution.
And directs how to attend upon it in a due manner.

The believer's triumph over death and the grave, An exhortation to diligence.
